records: ChEMBL1071707 (Morwick et al. 2010 ROCK2 luciferase assay; local Phase 18 curation)
PDB 6ED6 (ROCK2 inhibitor complex; structural overlap question)
scope.question: Can the published Boltz-2 sources establish row-level inclusion or exclusion of this assay, target, or structure in affinity pretraining?

sources.use: Training source families, affinity curation, structural date cutoff, benchmark leakage statement.
Documents separate affinity outputs and states that updated Boltz-2 training code is forthcoming in the archived official README.
Inference limits: affinity value is log10(IC50) in µM and is intended for comparison of active molecules; binary probability is a different supervision context.

ChEMBL assay identity and metadata used for the reviewed Phase 18 curation: human ROCK2, homogeneous luciferase, biochemical assay type, confidence score 9, target CHEMBL2973. This is evidence that the assay exists in ChEMBL, not evidence that Boltz-2 retained it.
Structure identity and release metadata; no row-level Boltz-2 membership manifest is published.

documented_training_facts.fact: Boltz-2 affinity regression draws primarily from PubChem, ChEMBL, and BindingDB; the paper reports aggregate counts, not a released per-row manifest.
documented_training_facts.evidence: Primary paper Data pp. 2-4 and Appendix A.2 pp. 19-22; ChEMBL v34 is named explicitly.

documented_training_facts.fact: ChEMBL extraction requires confidence score 9, SINGLE PROTEIN target type, biochemical or functional assay, supported affinity standard types, and exclusion of unreliable sources. Further assay-level ipTM, PAINS, heavy-atom, and distribution/size filters are applied.
documented_training_facts.evidence: Primary paper Appendix A.2, especially pp. 20-22.

documented_training_facts.fact: The continuous head mixes Ki, Kd, IC50, AC50, EC50, and XC50 after conversion to log10 with µM as reference. The public docs describe affinity_pred_value as log10(IC50) µM and recommend comparing active molecules.
documented_training_facts.evidence: Primary paper pp. 3-4; official docs README and prediction.md.

documented_training_facts.fact: PDB structural training uses structures released before 2023-06-01; the paper describes protein sequence clustering and held-out structural sets, but this is a structure-data rule and does not provide affinity-row membership.
documented_training_facts.evidence: Primary paper Data p. 2 and Appendix A.1 pp. 18-19.

documented_training_facts.fact: The paper says TYK2 was selected because it was in the affinity-model test set and avoided data leakage, showing that target-level split information matters for that benchmark. It does not publish an equivalent ROCK2 membership list.

direct_evidence: The assay is present in ChEMBL and local metadata identify confidence score 9, a human ROCK2 homogeneous luciferase biochemical assay (CHEMBL2973).
The published Boltz-2 recipe names ChEMBL v34 and filters that are superficially compatible with this metadata.
why_eligibility_is_not_membership: The published recipe does not report retained assay IDs or ligand rows.
Retention depends on additional assay-level structure-confidence and chemical/distribution filters; exact values and standardized structures are unavailable in the paper.
The Morwick assay has a known luciferase-interference caveat in the source audit, but the paper does not say whether this particular assay or its compounds was manually removed.
ChEMBL presence and source-version naming cannot establish inclusion in a released checkpoint or identify whether a given row was used for a particular head/split.
CHEMBL1071707_Morwick2010.inference: It is plausible that some records could have been eligible for extraction, but no defensible probability or membership claim can be made from the available primary sources.

ROCK2_O75116.direct_evidence: The paper reports aggregate target-cluster counts and source families only; it does not list UniProt IDs, ChEMBL target IDs, assay IDs, or target-cluster assignments for training/test affinity data.
ROCK2_O75116.inference: Neither presence nor absence of human ROCK2/O75116 in affinity training can be established. A target being represented in ChEMBL v34 is not proof that any of its assays survived curation.

PDB_6ED6.structural_candidate_status: likely eligible by release date, membership unknown
PDB_6ED6.direct_evidence: 6ED6 is a public ROCK2 complex released before the paper's 2023-06-01 structural cutoff (official RCSB record).
PDB_6ED6.inference: Release before the cutoff makes it a candidate for structural data processing, but resolution, ligand similarity, clustering, random subsampling, and any final training-set selection cannot be checked against a published manifest.

limits_and_required_validation: The paper and official repository materials do not expose a row-level affinity training manifest, exact ChEMBL extraction date beyond v34, checkpoint-to-row map, or target/ligand membership query.
Do not label the Phase 18 ROCK2 evaluation as an unseen-model holdout. It is a cross-publication retrospective evaluation with training overlap unknown.

A strict independence claim requires a provider-supplied training manifest/attestation or an auditable checkpoint data release mapping assay IDs, standardized ligand identities, target sequences, and split assignments. Source publication date alone is insufficient.

If overlap cannot be resolved, report the evaluation as transfer/generalization evidence conditional on unknown pretraining overlap; retain the frozen assay curation and report luciferase-interference and assay-context limitations.
Do not infer experimental efficacy, novelty, or prospective discovery from affinity predictions, regardless of whether a ROCK2 record was or was not in training.
conclusion: Available primary sources establish the data families, broad filters, and structural cutoff, but cannot establish inclusion or exclusion of CHEMBL1071707, ROCK2/O75116, or PDB 6ED6 in the Boltz-2 affinity training set. Exact overlap remains unknown and must be treated as a material provenance limitation.
